category: residential egress: rotating residential, static residential, dedicated mobile

free_tier.stated: 'Try residential and mobile proxies for $1.97' - a paid trial, not a free allowance.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: a byte stream and an address, not an object

retention.stated: not applicable: a live endpoint, not stored bytes

egress.terms: The page title states the three headline rates: 'Residential $1.50/GB, Mobile $2/GB, ISP $2/IP'; the body adds 'unused GB roll over' and, for dedicated mobile, 'unlimited bandwidth and unlimited IP changes on demand'.
egress.price_per_tb: USD 1.50/GB residential, i.e. USD 1,536 per TiB; USD 2.00/IP/month for static ISP; mobile metered at $2/GB or unlimited on a dedicated port

interface_detail: HTTP(S) and SOCKS5 with country, region, city, ZIP, ISP, ASN and OS targeting on the rotating products; a fixed address on the static residential and dedicated mobile products.
chaining: The cheapest credible metered residential rate found ($1.50/GB) and, separately, a $2/month static ISP address and a dedicated mobile port with unlimited bandwidth: one vendor showing all three price shapes side by side, which is why the 'residential egress' question cannot be answered with a single $/GB number.

limits.value: rotating products are metered and roll unused GB over; the static ISP and dedicated mobile products are sold per address or port with no meter

limits_note: Unused GB rolling over changes the arithmetic for a bursty workload but not for a steady 1 TiB month, which spends the allowance every month by construction.
binding_note: For the metered product the allowance is the binding constraint at USD 1,536 a TiB; for the $2 static ISP address nothing in the vocabulary binds and the terms of the debrid service become the limit.

identity_cost.detail: Self-service account with card; the trial costs $1.97 rather than requiring a free registration.

confidence_note: The three headline rates are in the page title and the body, read today. The per-product detail pages were not opened, so the exact terms behind 'unlimited bandwidth' on the mobile port are untested.

evidence.proved: title 'Proxy Pricing: Residential $1.50/GB, Mobile $2/GB, ISP $2/IP'; 'Try residential and mobile proxies for $1.97'; 'unused GB roll over'; dedicated mobile 'unlimited bandwidth and unlimited IP changes on demand'; '30M+ ... residential IPs' and '24 Countries' for static residential

notes: Included because it is the only vendor read that prices all three shapes on one page: metered residential, static ISP and unlimited dedicated mobile. That is the evidence that 'what a residential IP costs' has three answers, not one.
